segments.text: ​​​ ​Shiori~n!​ ​​

​​​ ​Are you ready to live​ ​​
​​ ​vicariously through m-m-me?!​ ​​
​​​ ​If that's the case, then welcome aboard​ ​​
​​​ ​to our seven-day trip on​ ​​
​​​ ​the Royal Caribbean Cruise Ship.​ ​​

​​​ ​Following an extensive,​ ​​
​​ ​questionably long voyage​ ​​
​​​ ​involving air and land travel,​ ​​
​​​ ​we finally arrive at the vibrant port​ ​​

​​​ ​where my floating Petri dish​ ​​
​​ ​of a prison awaits.​ ​​
​​​ ​Witness the splendor of the ship's interior​ ​​

​​​ ​with all its legal proceedings so​ ​​
​​ ​no one gets sued or hurt.​ ​​
​​​ ​The first day of this trip revolved around​ ​​
​​​ ​exploring every nook and cranny of the ship​ ​​
​​​ ​with this majestic vessel.​ ​​
​​​ ​The heart of activity is around Deck 5,​ ​​

​​​ ​which is basically the​ ​​
​​ ​equivalent of a Dark Souls hub.​ ​​
​​​ ​Moving on from Deck 5...​ ​​
​​​ ​So if you add number 1 to that,​ ​​
​​​ ​that becomes Deck 6...​ ​​
​​​ ​You get the enchanting boardwalk,​ ​​
​​​ ​with Deck 8 having a delightful mini park.​ ​​
​​​ ​And by that, I mean not an amusement park,​ ​​
​​​ ​but the one where you walk your dogs.​ ​​
​​​ ​FuwaMoco, hello!​ ​​
​​​ ​Deck 16 has a bar!​ ​​
​​​ ​But I don't drink alcohol so no footage​ ​​
​​​ ​And then you can indulge in breathtaking views​ ​​
​​​ ​and even skywalk.​ ​​
​​​ ​If you really, really...​ ​​
​​​ ​Actually, what's it called? Skyline?​ ​​

​​​ ​That thing where you stand at​ ​​
​​ ​the edge of, like, a cliff,​ ​​
​​​ ​but there's a pole,​ ​​
​​​ ​and it has a long rope,​ ​​
​​​ ​and you go down that rope.​ ​​
​​​ ​But you have a pulley...​ ​​
​​​ ​Skylining!​ ​​
​​​ ​Skylining...?​ ​​
​​​ ​I don't know, but you just​ ​​
​​​ ​drop down and try not to go kaput.​ ​​
​​​ ​Besides that, let's talk food.​ ​​

​​​ ​Every single day on the ship was​ ​​
​​ ​basically a food festival.​ ​​

​​​ ​The buffets were open​ ​​
​​ ​from 8:30 to 2PM for lunch.​ ​​
​​​ ​There were pizza joints and even cafés open​ ​​
​​​ ​that served complimentary food up until 2AM.​ ​​
​​​ ​And they had a classy dining room situation​ ​​
​​​ ​where you can just sit down​ ​​
​​​ ​and have a fancy three-course meal or more.​ ​​
​​​ ​Because...​ ​​
​​​ ​Oh boy, they really let you order more.​ ​​
​​​ ​My relatives went out on all these food options​ ​​

​​​ ​that by the third day I was​ ​​
​​ ​pretty fed up from eating.​ ​​
​​​ ​Every five hours, they wanted to eat.​ ​​
​​​ ​I don't know what was wrong with their metabolism,​ ​​
​​​ ​but, ugh!​ ​​
​​​ ​Good god!​ ​​
​​​ ​Good gravy!​ ​​

​​​ ​Here I am struggling just eating,​ ​​
​​ ​like, fricking two meals.​ ​​
​​​ ​Or let alone one. Like, what the heck?​ ​​
​​​ ​On the night of the first day,​ ​​
​​​ ​we watched an impressive ice skating show​ ​​

​​​ ​performed by skaters who performed​ ​​
​​ ​in international competitions.​ ​​
​​​ ​I don't remember their names,​ ​​

​​​ ​but just know that some of​ ​​
​​ ​them might've had medals.​ ​​
​​​ ​The level of skill and effort​ ​​

​​​ ​required to do so many tricks​ ​​
​​ ​is mind-boggling.​ ​​
​​​ ​I suppose it's kind of like watching​ ​​

​​​ ​an Italian plumber wearing​ ​​
​​ ​a red hat jump around,​ ​​
​​​ ​but on ice skates.​ ​​
​​​ ​It was very cool, honestly.​ ​​
​​​ ​The way that they lift each other up,​ ​​
​​​ ​do a 360 no scope...​ ​​
​​​ ​Like, wow.​ ​​
​​​ ​Can not relate to doing that,​ ​​
​​​ ​but I commend people who can.​ ​​
​​​ ​Day 2, we were stuck at sea.​ ​​
​​​ ​Inspired by the ice skating show,​ ​​

​​​ ​although knowing​ ​​
​​ ​I would not succeed at this,​ ​​
​​​ ​I tried to give ice skating a whirl.​ ​​
​​​ ​Unfortunately, I have no balance.​ ​​

​​​ ​For those who don't know, I don't​ ​​
​​ ​even know how to ride a bike.​ ​​

​​​ ​POV: Shiori just went out for a bit to​ ​​
​​ ​get some fresh air with her bicycle​ ​​
​​​ ​Absolutely no coordination.​ ​​
​​​ ​So I just clutched to the railings​ ​​
​​​ ​for the entirety of the time I had.​ ​​
​​​ ​The good news is that I didn't fall.​ ​​

​​​ ​The bad news was,​ ​​
​​ ​it did not feel fun,​ ​​
​​​ ​and my entire body was sore by the end of it​ ​​
​​​ ​just by trying to keep afloat.​ ​​

​​​ ​Moving on from my amazing​ ​​
​​ ​ice skating endeavors,​ ​​
​​​ ​the Nyakuza and I went to...!​ ​​
​​​ ​the casino for some good old gacha rolls.​ ​​

​​​ ​I'm not one to spend money​ ​​
​​ ​on these things, though.​ ​​

​​​ ​As you guys know,​ ​​
​​ ​I don't even spend on gacha,​ ​​

​​​ ​so I really just​ ​​
​​ ​stood there watching everyone​ ​​

​​​ ​gamble things away​ ​​
​​ ​while I was standing there.​ ​​
​​​ ​I stood there awkwardly​ ​​
​​​ ​while they gambled their savings away.​ ​​
​​​ ​Fire, fire, light the fire!​ ​​
​​​ ​Closing off the second day,​ ​​
​​​ ​there was an amazing, thrilling air of danger​ ​​
​​​ ​as we caught a water aria.​ ​​

​​​ ​Man, I don't know how much​ ​​
​​ ​these people are getting paid.​ ​​
​​​ ​Like, this is some amazing...​ ​​
​​​ ​whoo hee, hoo haha...​ ​​
​​​ ​tricks. Like, my good golly.​ ​​
​​​ ​Climb up a giant ladder, and they just​ ​​
​​​ ​hopefully make it to the pool.​ ​​
​​​ ​It's scary. It's terrifying.​ ​​

​​​ ​I... I hope they​ ​​
​​ ​get paid an amazing amount.​ ​​
​​​ ​The third day of this week-long voyage,​ ​​

​​​ ​I started feeling pretty guilty about​ ​​
​​ ​the amount of food I was having.​ ​​
​​​ ​Even if it wasn't my choice.​ ​​
​​​ ​So, I ended up going to the solarium​ ​​
​​​ ​for a nice dip in the pool.​ ​​
​​​ ​And no kids were allowed in here.​ ​​
​​​ ​But it was pretty awkward,​ ​​
​​​ ​because it was just a bunch of adults​ ​​

​​​ ​having martinis and alcohol​ ​​
​​ ​in their hands...​ ​​

​​​ ​And I'm just like, I kinda just didn't​ ​​
​​ ​wanna be around kids.​ ​​
​​​ ​And I was hoping it'd be a lot more empty.​ ​​
​​​ ​Basically, all the adults do is sit around,​ ​​
​​​ ​drinking their alchohool.​ ​​
​​​ ​And I'm just there,​ ​​
​​​ ​wishing I could have space to swim,​ ​​
​​​ ​but no one is swimming,​ ​​
​​​ ​so I'm there without alcohol just watching everyone.​ ​​
​​​ ​It was pretty awkward.​ ​​

​​​ ​I also managed to incorporate some​ ​​
​​ ​exercise into my day. Yeah!​ ​​
​​​ ​The ship had a gym.​ ​​
​​​ ​It was pretty empty.​ ​​

​​​ ​Which is honestly good​ ​​
​​ ​for me as an introvert.​ ​​

​​​ ​There was a treadmill,​ ​​
​​ ​and they had a PVP feature.​ ​​
​​​ ​Basically people who used it before,​ ​​

​​​ ​they have some sort of track record​ ​​
​​ ​for how long they walked.​ ​​

​​​ ​And now you could​ ​​
​​ ​virtually walk alongside them,​ ​​
​​​ ​or against them.​ ​​
​​​ ​I didn't really care.​ ​​

​​​ ​I don't care about who this​ ​​
​​ ​Mandy and this Billy is.​ ​​

​​​ ​I just wanted to walk in​ ​​
​​ ​virtual New York or something.​ ​​
​​​ ​The ship also had an outdoor track.​ ​​
​​​ ​But the windy weather was...​ ​​
​​​ ​Well, it was pretty windy.​ ​​
​​​ ​And the hot weather was...​ ​​
​​​ ​Well, it was pretty hot.​ ​​
​​​ ​Man, I honestly liked the gym.​ ​​
​​​ ​That was the best part of the cruise ship​ ​​
​​​ ​because there was no one there.​ ​​

​​​ ​There was, like,​ ​​
​​ ​one or three people there,​ ​​

​​​ ​and I was like,​ ​​
​​ ​"Oh yes, this is my heaven."​ ​​

​​​ ​Now, to the enchanting​ ​​
​​ ​fourth day of the journey.​ ​​
​​​ ​We reached the shores of our destination.​ ​​
​​​ ​Behold the quaint island home to​ ​​
​​​ ​basically 150,000 souls at max.​ ​​

​​​ ​And our tour guide taught us that​ ​​
​​ ​there's no running water here.​ ​​
​​​ ​If there was, it was a scarcity.​ ​​

​​​ ​And it was mostly a sanctuary for​ ​​
​​ ​endangered animal species.​ ​​
​​​ ​Without going into too much detail,​ ​​
​​​ ​one of them was a lizard.​ ​​

​​​ ​And you were not allowed​ ​​
​​ ​to hunt this lizard,​ ​​
​​​ ​but you could eat this lizard.​ ​​

​​​ ​So there was a little bit​ ​​
​​ ​of a loophole there somehow.​ ​​
​​​ ​During this, there was basically shopping...​ ​​
​​​ ​Oh, and hugging monkeys and embracing sloths.​ ​​
​​​ ​Which is probably why I might've gotten sick.​ ​​

​​​ ​The monkeys were hanging out​ ​​
​​ ​in a big gigantic cage​ ​​
​​​ ​that you could go into.​ ​​

​​​ ​And don't worry,​ ​​
​​ ​they did not wrestle with you.​ ​​

​​​ ​But we were warned that​ ​​
​​ ​they might steal from you,​ ​​
​​​ ​cause they were little kleptomaniacs.​ ​​

​​​ ​You had to be careful with​ ​​
​​ ​how you acted around them.​ ​​

​​​ ​If you panicked, well, they might​ ​​
​​ ​smack the crap out of you​ ​​
​​​ ​and go, like, "Oo! Ee! Oo aa aa!"​ ​​

​​​ ​There was a few monkeys​ ​​
​​ ​that had a day off.​ ​​

​​​ ​And by that,​ ​​
​​ ​I mean they were released from the cage​ ​​

​​​ ​so they don't have to​ ​​
​​ ​awkwardly steal crap from you and​ ​​
​​​ ​jump on your head.​ ​​

​​​ ​But the one that​ ​​
​​ ​I saw that had a day off,​ ​​
​​​ ​it had a head injury.​ ​​
​​​ ​And then there was another monkey performing​ ​​
​​​ ​some sort of checkup on it,​ ​​
​​​ ​or it was eating its brains.​ ​​
​​​ ​I'm not entirely sure.​ ​​
​​​ ​But I like to think it was cannibalism.​ ​​
​​​ ​The monkeys were pretty touchy.​ ​​
​​​ ​They were jumping on everyone's heads.​ ​​
​​​ ​They touched my hand...​ ​​

​​​ ​It was only once.​ ​​
​​ ​It was a fraction of a second.​ ​​
​​​ ​But it was the softest paws I've ever felt.​ ​​
​​​ ​Don't tell my cats. They might get jealous.​ ​​
​​​ ​But my good golly.​ ​​
​​​ ​They have really nice hands for creatures​ ​​
​​​ ​that use hands to travel.​ ​​
​​​ ​I kind of wonder if it was the monkey​ ​​
​​​ ​that was eating the brains of its friends,​ ​​
​​​ ​but I hope not.​ ​​
​​​ ​But if it was...​ ​​

​​​ ​Well, it's no wonder I got sick,​ ​​
​​ ​'cause it had germs.​ ​​
​​​ ​Apart from the monkey encounters,​ ​​
​​​ ​we also got to hug a sloth.​ ​​
​​​ ​The sloth's fur did not feel pretty good.​ ​​
​​​ ​It was, like, dry... coarse...​ ​​
​​​ ​And it gets everywhere.​ ​​
​​​ ​It was not pleasant.​ ​​

​​​ ​Essentially,​ ​​
​​ ​I assume if you take a hairball...​ ​​

​​​ ​It could be yours,​ ​​
​​ ​or your cat's...​ ​​

​​​ ​And if you dried it up​ ​​
​​ ​in a microwave or an oven,​ ​​
​​​ ​I assume that's what it feels like.​ ​​
​​​ ​Or an extra dry coconut.​ ​​
​​​ ​I mean, I liked holding the sloth, though.​ ​​

​​​ ​But you know,​ ​​
​​ ​the sloth also could've made me sick.​ ​​
​​​ ​I felt pretty bad for the sloth, though,​ ​​
​​​ ​because it was kind of getting manhandled.​ ​​

​​​ ​But sloths have really impressive arm​ ​​
​​ ​strength from what I'm aware,​ ​​
​​​ ​so maybe the way it was manhandled was, like,​ ​​
​​​ ​a feathery touch to it for all I know.​ ​​
​​​ ​The end of the fourth day was basically going​ ​​
​​​ ​to a mini submarine.​ ​​

​​​ ​We got to look at the ocean floor​ ​​
​​ ​with its colorful coral reefs.​ ​​
​​​ ​And by that, I mean it wasn't very colorful.​ ​​
​​​ ​It was more like just yellow.​ ​​

​​​ ​But they told me that​ ​​
​​ ​it would be dazzling at night.​ ​​
​​​ ​However, I cannot verify that,​ ​​

​​​ ​for I don't want to go into​ ​​
​​ ​the middle of the ocean at night.​ ​​
​​​ ​Day 5 and 6 was essentially...​ ​​
​​​ ​shopping!​ ​​
​​​ ​Docking at a bustling port for day 5.​ ​​

​​​ ​Thanks to the advice of Novelites,​ ​​
​​ ​I packed enough underwear.​ ​​
​​​ ​However, for my lack of foresight,​ ​​
​​​ ​I didn't pack enough clothes.​ ​​
​​​ ​But you know, I had a lot of underwear.​ ​​
​​​ ​As fate would have it,​ ​​
​​​ ​I had to endure the sweltering, sticky weather​ ​​
​​​ ​wearing the ultimate nemesis:​ ​​

​​​ ​And not just any pants,​ ​​
​​ ​but they were black pants.​ ​​
​​​ ​The kind that absorbs heat like a sponge,​ ​​

​​​ ​smacking you around as if you were​ ​​
​​ ​a wacky inflatable tube man​ ​​

​​​ ​waving in the wind​ ​​
​​ ​without a care in the world.​ ​​
​​​ ​So day 5 consisted of shopping,​ ​​

​​​ ​and I grabbed a ragdoll​ ​​
​​ ​from one of the shops.​ ​​

​​​ ​I don't remember making​ ​​
​​ ​any other purchases than this,​ ​​

​​​ ​because the rest of the day,​ ​​
​​ ​I had a tension headache,​ ​​
​​​ ​and I just stayed in bed,​ ​​
​​​ ​and I had a fever dream.​ ​​
​​​ ​The dream was, they couldn't bring pizza​ ​​
​​​ ​to the third floor of my dorm​ ​​
​​​ ​Tangent Time​ ​​

​​​ ​because there was a student​ ​​
​​ ​that used to live there,​ ​​

​​​ ​and he was cheese-grated to oblivion​ ​​
​​ ​by the school principal.​ ​​
​​​ ​And his ghost would haunt anyone​ ​​

​​​ ​who dared bring delicious cheese-filled​ ​​
​​ ​tomato-sputtered pizza​ ​​
​​​ ​to that floor.​ ​​
​​​ ​It kind of became surreal from that point,​ ​​

​​​ ​because then I dreamt that​ ​​
​​ ​I was streaming in a car,​ ​​
​​​ ​and Beauty and "East" made an appearance.​ ​​
​​​ ​And the "East" was wearing a wifebeater shirt.​ ​​

​​​ ​And let's just say,​ ​​
​​ ​he did not treat Beauty that well.​ ​​
​​​ ​I don't know exactly what he did,​ ​​
​​​ ​but she seemed pretty unhappy.​ ​​
​​​ ​And then I received a text from my manager.​ ​​
​​​ ​And he said, like,​ ​​

​​​ ​"Hey, Shiori, you better not​ ​​
​​ ​show copyrighted movies​ ​​
​​​ ​for this movie watchalong."​ ​​
​​​ ​And I said "Oops."​ ​​

​​​ ​And I immediately thought,​ ​​
​​ ​"I guess this is getting privated."​ ​​

​​​ ​All of a sudden, Sherlock Holmes​ ​​
​​ ​appears as my bodyguard,​ ​​

​​​ ​trailing behind me in a vintage​ ​​
​​ ​black-and-white rendition of himself​ ​​
​​​ ​as if he was starring in a movie from the 1900's.​ ​​
​​​ ​So yeah, it was basically a normal dream.​ ​​
​​​ ​Day 6. Guess what?​ ​​
​​​ ​More shopping!​ ​​
​​​ ​So we arrived at another bustling port​ ​​

​​​ ​where two trusty tour guides led​ ​​
​​ ​us to a store hopping spree.​ ​​
​​​ ​The first store was a general store,​ ​​
​​​ ​and there was a bunch of goods.​ ​​
​​​ ​I guess, like, Day of the Dead souvenirs.​ ​​

​​​ ​I really liked this.​ ​​
​​ ​The Skelebros were really cool to look at.​ ​​
​​​ ​I really wanted to buy more,​ ​​
​​​ ​but, you know, that's...​ ​​
​​​ ​That's a little bit too much archiving.​ ​​
​​​ ​However, I did pick up a doll.​ ​​
​​​ ​The final store was the tea store,​ ​​

​​​ ​which is another reason​ ​​
​​ ​that I might've gotten sick.​ ​​
​​​ ​So they had several tea samples.​ ​​
​​​ ​The first being their famous Happy Tea.​ ​​
​​​ ​Oddly enough, after taking a sip of this​ ​​
​​​ ​seemingly innocent concoction,​ ​​
​​​ ​that was when my throat started feeling itchy.​ ​​
​​​ ​And scratchy.​ ​​

​​​ ​And I wondered,​ ​​
​​ ​is this really health friendly as they claim?​ ​​

​​​ ​Because instead of my health​ ​​
​​ ​becoming a positive slope,​ ​​
​​​ ​it became inversed.​ ​​

​​​ ​So untrue to its name,​ ​​
​​ ​the tea did not make me happy.​ ​​
​​​ ​I got sick the following week and a half,​ ​​
​​​ ​and I still have a dry cough to this day.​ ​​
​​​ ​That same night,​ ​​

​​​ ​after the usual three-course meal​ ​​
​​ ​in the formal dining room,​ ​​
​​​ ​we watched Guardians of the Galaxy 3​ ​​
​​​ ​in the ship's theater room.​ ​​
​​​ ​Fun movie, by the way.​ ​​
​​​ ​I also ship Nebula and the main character.​ ​​
​​​ ​Don't change my mind.​ ​​
​​​ ​Sorry, Gamora, but Nebula's pretty nice.​ ​​

​​​ ​And then day 7​ ​​
​​ ​is basically the end of the trip.​ ​​
​​​ ​Flew back home,​ ​​
​​​ ​drove back home...​ ​​
​​​ ​But not me driving.​ ​​
​​​ ​And now, I'm back to where I belong:​ ​​

​​​ ​in the basement,​ ​​
​​ ​in my four-padded safe room.​ ​​
